insights.content: US iGaming legalization outlook for 2026: Maine already approved (1.4M population, 8th state for online casino). Virginia (8.7M) and Indiana (6.7M) seen as likely candidates. New York (20M population) would be transformative - Senator Adabo pushing hard with fourth consecutive annual proposal at 30.5% tax rate. Combined legalization of Indiana + Virginia + New York would create 'catch-up effect' the market has anticipated for 5 years.
insights.speaker: Erik Lundberg

insights.content: Danish companies tend to guide conservatively and then beat expectations with upward revisions, unlike some other markets. This pattern seen in Trophy Games and Hov - described as 'Finnish guidance' (very conservative) rather than typical Danish over-promising.
insights.speaker: Marcus Gadda

insights.content: Operating leverage is powerful in platform businesses: Free Trailer showed 14.9% rental growth translating to 26% revenue growth and 36% EBIT growth in Q3. 'Simple math' - more trailers equals better offering equals better moat.
insights.speaker: Erik Lundberg

insights.content: Fastest growing iGaming markets globally according to Blask data: Greece (#17), Saudi Arabia (#20 - surprising given assumed strict laws), and Philippines (#12). UK remains largest overall market, with Italy close behind.
insights.speaker: Erik Lundberg

insights.content: Tax policy on gambling matters critically: Colombia's 19% VAT on player deposits caused 30% GGR decline and was completely unsustainable. Now switching to GGR-based taxation which is healthier for industry. Brazil also considering similar deposit tax despite Colombia's failure - 'should look at neighbor country'.
insights.speaker: Erik Lundberg

insights.content: On insider selling: Many VDs/entrepreneurs start from nothing with 100% equity - they should absolutely be allowed to take money off the table after success. Example given of buying houses and renovating. Insider buys are more meaningful signals than sells. Small 'dutting' purchases by executives with million-dollar salaries (like Tim Cook at Apple) are meaningless to read into.
insights.speaker: Erik Lundberg

insights.content: Most common retail investor mistake: Making it too complicated. 'I det enkla ligger det vackra' (In simplicity lies beauty) - quoting Ernst Kirchsteiger. Over-analysis and taking investment theses too many steps too far.
insights.speaker: Erik Lundberg

insights.content: It is absolutely possible to beat index over time with normal IQ and strong interest. All academic theory says it's impossible due to efficient market hypothesis, but with knowledge, time commitment, sound thinking, and learning from mistakes it can be done. Key is avoiding leverage and 'idiot bets'.
insights.speaker: Erik Lundberg

insights.content: Nigeria is a much larger iGaming market than expected: estimated $1.5-2.5B GGR, roughly half of Brazil's regulated market ($4-6B). Africa payments have leapfrogged from cash directly to mobile/crypto, skipping card infrastructure entirely. Tunisia also surprisingly important for Evolution.
insights.speaker: Erik Lundberg

insights.content: On Twitter/FinTwit behavior: Be polite and open - incredible people hide behind anonymous accounts (electricians, Willys purchasers) who provide valuable insights on iGaming, legal interpretations, etc. Give and take. Respect different investment time horizons - not everyone is Buffett holding forever. 'All long-term holdings are short-term holdings that went badly' should be avoided.

insights.content: If starting from scratch with portfolio wiped: Would invest in Swedish small-caps, specifically mentioned Infracom as solid choice. Would need to reflect on what went wrong but core strategy remains Swedish small-caps.

summary: Episode 270 celebrates Erik's birthday with a mix of Danish portfolio updates, US iGaming regulatory outlook, and an entertaining stock tournament. The hosts remain highly bullish on their Danish holdings (Hov, Free Trailer) which show strong operating leverage and conservative management guidance. Erik provides extensive iGaming analysis covering US state legalization prospects (Maine passed, Virginia/Indiana/New York likely 2026 candidates) and surprising growth markets (Saudi Arabia, Philippines). A 16-stock tournament results in Generic winning over Carrium in the final, with C-Tech and Infracom as other semifinalists.
key_takeaways: Danish portfolio holdings (Hov at 5x EBITDA, Free Trailer with 22% fleet growth) remain core convictions with conservative management guidance suggesting upside
US iGaming could see significant progress in 2026: Maine passed, New York Senator Adabo pushing fourth annual proposal - combined legalization would create long-awaited catch-up effect
Operating leverage in platform businesses is powerful: Free Trailer's 15% rental growth translates to 26% revenue and 36% EBIT growth
Stock tournament winner Generic (e-commerce software) and runner-up Carrium (personal alarms) seen as attractive risk/reward plays
Keep investing simple - overanalysis is the most common retail investor mistake according to the hosts
